CANONICAL_NAME.value: Viterbi / HMM decoder (compact C++ reference, Min Xu)

VERSION.value: github.com/xukmin/viterbi master as of 2026-09-12 (commit in hashes)

value.lineage: The Viterbi algorithm (1967) over a Hidden Markov Model (Rabiner 1989): find the most-likely hidden state path for an observation sequence by dynamic programming over the trellis; this is a small, tested C++ reference of the HMM + Viterbi decode

HUMAN_PROBLEM.value: most-likely-path inference in a hidden Markov model (Viterbi)

value.built_to: recover the most-likely sequence of hidden states that produced an observed sequence, by dynamic programming over the HMM trellis (predict-then-max at each step)
value.pressure: the true state sequence is never observed, only noisy emissions; the number of possible paths is exponential in sequence length
value.success_means: the decoded path matches the true generating states on the test HMM; likelihood computed correctly

value.pressure: hidden state, noisy/ambiguous emissions, exponential path space
value.failure_condition: a wrong transition/emission model yields a wrong decoded path -- a speech recogniser or gene finder built on it makes systematic errors
